title: より, のほう and 一方
summary: より marks the baseline of a comparison, ほう is a noun meaning "side", and 一方 means "one side": it opens a contrast or a steady one-way trend.

blocks.text: Textbooks teach より and ほう together in one sentence, which hides what each does. Learn them separately first.

**より** means "from" in the sense of distance from a point. Used as a baseline, it says "measured from here". It is not a case particle, so it can follow nouns, clauses, verbs and adjectives. (**から** is the "starting point" one: 日本から来た.)

blocks.jp: さくらはメアリーよりきれいだ。
今年の冬はいつもより寒い。
blocks.en: This winter is colder than usual.

blocks.text: Note that the sentence does not say Mary is not pretty. より only sets a reference point.
**ほう** is a noun: a direction or **side**. If there is one side, there is another, so it fits comparisons: Xのほう is "the X side".

blocks.jp: 肉より魚のほうが好きだ。
blocks.en: I like fish better than meat.

blocks.jp: バスより電車のほうが速い。
blocks.en: The train is faster than the bus.

blocks.text: Either part can be dropped when the comparison is clear. Using both adds emphasis or formality.

**一方** is literally "one side". In narration it turns to the opposite side of the story: "meanwhile, on the other hand". After an adjective it makes a contrast. After a plain verb + だ it means "only going one way".

blocks.jp: この辺りは静かな一方で、不便だ。
blocks.en: This area is quiet, but on the other hand it is inconvenient.

items: **AよりB**: B compared with baseline A.
**Xのほう**: the X side; used to pick one in a comparison.
**Verb + 一方だ**: keeps going in one direction.

questions.instruction: Which is the baseline of the comparison?
questions.prompt: このかばんは、あのかばんより安い。
questions.note: より marks the baseline.
questions.en: This bag is cheaper than that bag.

questions.instruction: Which season do I like better?
questions.prompt: 私は夏より冬のほうが好きだ。
questions.note: Xのほうが picks the preferred side.
questions.en: I like winter better than summer.

questions.note: より sets the baseline.
questions.en: I like cats better than dogs.

questions.note: より: baseline.
questions.en: My younger brother is taller than me.

questions.note: Xのほうが picks one side.
questions.en: A car is more convenient than a train.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says tea is preferred over coffee?
options: コーヒーよりお茶のほうが好きだ。
お茶よりコーヒーのほうが好きだ。
お茶もコーヒーも好きだ。
お茶のコーヒーが好きだ。
questions.note: The ほう side is the one chosen.

questions.instruction: What does 一方 do here?
questions.prompt: 仕事は忙しい一方で、楽しい。
questions.note: 一方で opens the other side.
questions.en: Work is busy, but on the other hand it is fun.

questions.prompt: 最近、夏は暑くなる一方だ。
options: It is hotter than before only today
It keeps getting hotter, in one direction
questions.note: Verb + 一方だ: one direction only.
questions.en: Summers just keep getting hotter these days.

questions.prompt: より says the baseline is bad.
questions.note: より only sets a reference point.

questions.instruction: What does ほう mean in 電車のほう?
questions.note: ほう is a noun: a side.

options: 日本は中国より小さい。
日本は小さい中国より。
questions.note: The baseline comes before より, in front of the engine.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I got up earlier than usual"?
options: いつもより遅く起きた。
いつもより早く起きた。
いつもは早く起きない。
questions.note: いつも is the baseline.

questions.instruction: What does 一方 link here?
questions.prompt: 田中さんは歌が上手な一方、ダンスはにがてだ。
questions.note: 一方 contrasts the other side.
questions.en: Mr. Tanaka is good at singing, but on the other hand he is bad at dancing.

options: 家より駅のほうが近い。
questions.note: より + ほう compare two things.
Topic, baseline, adjective.

questions.prompt: I like tea better than juice.
questions.note: Baseline より, then Xのほうが.
questions.en: I like tea better than juice.

questions.prompt: This room is quieter than that room.
questions.note: Baseline + より.
questions.en: This room is quieter than that room.

questions.prompt: The number of people in this town just keeps shrinking.
questions.note: Verb + 一方だ.
questions.en: The number of people in this town just keeps shrinking.

questions.prompt: My bag is heavier than yours.
questions.note: Baseline + より, then the adjective.
questions.en: My bag is heavier than yours.

questions.instruction: Tap the baseline of the comparison
questions.note: より marks the baseline.
ほう is a noun: a side.
questions.en: Meat is more expensive than fish.

questions.instruction: Tap the part that means "on the other hand"
questions.note: 一方で opens the other side.
questions.en: Japanese is interesting, but on the other hand it is hard.
